headline: Speed is distance over time—how fast you're going depends on both what you cover and how long it takes
universal_truth: Speed isn't just about moving fast; it's about the relationship between distance and time; efficiency matters
fun_facts: Light travels at 670,616,629 mph—the universal speed limit
A snail moves at about 0.03 mph; a cheetah at about 70 mph
The speed of sound varies—it's faster in water than in air, and even faster in steel
discussion_questions: Are you moving fast enough toward your goals?
When is speed helpful and when is it harmful?
What would 'faster' look like in an area you care about?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A cheetah moves at 70 mph. Light moves at 670 million mph. Speed is how much distance you cover in how much time. It's the ratio that matters—not just distance, not just time, but their relationship.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often focus on how far we've gone or how long we've worked. But speed combines both. What does thinking about speed reveal?
cliff.prompt: Why does speed matter as a concept?

options.text: Speed reveals efficiency—how much progress per unit time—which helps you compare approaches and optimize how you achieve goals
options.response: Yes. Speed = Distance / Time. Two people can travel the same distance but at different speeds. Two approaches can require the same effort but produce different speeds of progress.
Sometimes, but speed has costs—accuracy, depth, sustainability...

q1.title: The Speed Formula
q1.script: Speed equals distance divided by time. To go faster, cover more ground—or do it in less time. Both levers work. Sometimes efficiency gains are easier than effort increases.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Speed Formula"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Speed vs Velocity
q2.script: Speed is how fast; velocity includes direction. You can be moving fast but in the wrong direction—high speed, wrong velocity. In life, make sure you're going fast toward the right destination.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Sustainable Speed
q3.script: Sprint speed and marathon pace are different. Maximum speed isn't sustainable. Finding the speed you can maintain matters more than occasional bursts. Sustainable speed beats fast burnout.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Speed isn't just moving fast—it's the relationship between distance and time. Check your direction, find sustainable pace, and optimize for speed that lasts.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 223. Tomorrow, we'll explore acceleration—speeding up and slowing down. Until then, evaluate your speed toward one goal.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Speed Check - Progress Per Time
growTrack.activity: Pick a goal. How much progress have you made in the last month? Is that speed sufficient to reach your goal in your timeframe? Could you go faster by working differently (not just harder)? Speed is about efficiency, not just effort.
